questions.stem: The correct routine processing sequence after fixation is:
questions.explanation: Water is removed by graded alcohol, alcohol is replaced by a clearing agent, and clearing agent is replaced by paraffin.

questions.stem: Cloudy xylene in a processor most strongly indicates:
questions.explanation: Water entering the clearing station commonly produces a cloudy appearance and compromises clearing.

questions.stem: A fatty breast specimen remains soft after processing. The most appropriate investigation begins with:

choices.text: Specimen thickness and processing schedule adequacy

questions.explanation: Fatty or thick tissue may require improved grossing and a validated schedule with sufficient dehydration, clearing, and infiltration.

questions.stem: Brittle, shrunken tissue from multiple cassettes most strongly suggests:
questions.explanation: Excessive dehydration, prolonged processing, or high heat can harden and shrink tissue.

questions.stem: The safest way to establish a new overnight processor schedule is to:

choices.text: Validate representative tissue types and thicknesses
Use the longest possible times without review

questions.explanation: A schedule should be validated with representative tissues, sizes, and downstream requirements.

questions.stem: Paraffin infiltration is poor even though dehydration and clearing are adequate. The first processor variable to review is:
questions.explanation: Infiltration depends on clean paraffin at an appropriate validated temperature and effective pressure/vacuum cycles.

questions.stem: Strong-acid decalcification is most likely to compromise:
questions.explanation: Strong acids can rapidly remove calcium but may damage morphology, antigenicity, DNA, and RNA.

questions.stem: Many blocks show residual alcohol odor and poor paraffin support. The most likely failed step is:
questions.explanation: Incomplete clearing leaves alcohol in tissue and prevents effective paraffin infiltration.

questions.stem: The goal of correct embedding orientation is to:

choices.text: Present the diagnostically important surface first

questions.explanation: Orientation should expose the relevant tissue plane early and preserve relationships needed for interpretation.

questions.stem: A skin punch should generally be embedded so that the section shows:

choices.text: Epidermis through deep dermis in cross-section
The punch lying flat on its circular face

questions.explanation: A perpendicular cross-section demonstrates the full epithelial and dermal depth.
